title: NVSHMEM-backed shared KV-slab + staged allreduce bridge for low-latency TP workloads
author: Ravi Menon
description:
Motivation: Tensor-parallel (TP) workloads with many small key-value lookups suffer measurable cross-node latency when communicating per-token KV slices via NCCL collectives, especially on 8+ node clusters with small per-request payloads. This PR introduces an optional NVSHMEM-backed shared slab for hot KV pages and a staged allreduce bridge that (1) reduces host-to-device handshake overhead for small shards, (2) lets nodes perform lock-free reads from a shared slab where hardware permits, and (3) performs a lightweight staged allreduce that only moves compacted/compressible chunks when full reduce semantics are not required immediately.

Design: - NVSHMEM shared-slab allocator: a contiguous slab region that holds hot KV pages in compressed (LZ4-lite) form. Slab metadata lives in a small NVSHMEM-resident header that uses sequence counters for wait-free handoff. - Read path: TP runtime probes NVSHMEM first for a KV slice; on hit it decompresses in-place and populates per-GPU cache lines without a full NCCL rendezvous. On miss, normal NCCL allgather/allreduce path executes. - Staged allreduce bridge: for gradient-less KV reads (inference-only), we use a size/entropy heuristic to decide between immediate NCCL allreduce for large/opaque shards vs. staged bridge for small/compressible shards. The staged bridge performs peer-to-peer NVSHMEM copy followed by a light aggregate step that uses an ephemeral CUDA kernel to merge chunked deltas. - Fallbacks: - If NVSHMEM is unsupported (older CUDA/driver) the runtime falls back to NCCL-only path. - If slab pressure is high, eviction demotes to NCCL path.

Implementation notes: - New components: src/runtime/collectives/nvshmem_bridge.cpp, src/runtime/kv/kvcache_shared_slab.{h,cpp}, src/runtime/kv/slab_eviction_policy.cpp - Heuristics tuned: compression threshold, chunk size (defaults: 32KB chunks, 12% entropy threshold), spin/timeout on NVSHMEM header prior to fallback. - Safety: sequence counters + epoch tags to ensure readers never see torn compressed headers; unit tests simulate concurrent reads/writes and NVSHMEM driver restarts.

Tests and CI: - Unit tests: tests/unit/test_shared_slab_eviction.cpp, tests/unit/test_nvshmem_header_consistency.cpp - Integration: tests/integration/test_nvshmem_kvcache.py runs a 4-node TP scenario in CI emulation (GHA job with loopback NVSHMEM sim) - Benchmarks: scripts/benchmarks/nvshmem_runner.py and perf results included under perf/nvshmem/ - CI: initial flake on Ubuntu-latest GPU job due to driver mismatch; pinned to CUDA 12.3 runner and rerun.

Performance: - 8x16-GPU TP cluster synthetic small-token stream: median per-token latency reduced 18% (from 12.3ms -> 10.1ms) and p99 reduced 22%. - End-to-end RLHF-ish chat eval (multi-turn, cache-friendly prompts): throughput improvement 14% and 11% lower inter-node bandwidth egress due to compression-aware chunking. - Microbenchmarks show NVSHMEM-hit latency for a 16KB shard ~40-60us vs NCCL-based gather ~210-260us.

Risks & mitigations: - NVSHMEM availability: guarded behind config flag and runtime autodetect. - Correctness: thorough deterministic tests and eviction/invalidation hooks; added a debug dump to verify slab contents post-merge. - Observability: added metrics (kvcache.nvshmem.hits, kvcache.nvshmem.evictions, kvcache.staged_bridge.count) and tracing spans for slab probes and staged merges.

Release notes: - Experimental NVSHMEM-backed shared KV slab and staged allreduce bridge to reduce TP inference latency for small shards. Opt-in behind --enable-nvshmem-kvcache flag.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc (docs/arch/collectives.md) - [x] Implementation - [x] Unit & integration tests - [x] Perf harness and baseline numbers - [x] Metrics and tracing changes - [x] Feature flag + fallback path
commit_summary: Implemented NVSHMEM shared slab and staged allreduce bridge, added heuristics for compression-aware chunking, tests, metrics, and perf harness. Fallback to NCCL when NVSHMEM unavailable.
commits: feat(collectives): add NVSHMEM bridge and staged merge kernel
feat(kv): shared slab allocator and LZ4-lite compressor for hot KV pages
test: add deterministic unit tests for NVSHMEM header counters and eviction
perf: add nvshmem_runner benchmark and baseline results
review_comments: Asha Patel: Can you clarify failure modes if a writer crashes while holding the NVSHMEM slab header? Suggest adding a tombstone + reclamation window.
Ravi Menon: Added tombstone epoch and reclamation window (30s default) and a debug flag to force immediate reclamation for test harness.
Miguel Torres: The entropy threshold seems aggressive for some LLM datasets; can we expose it as a per-model knob and document safe defaults?
Ravi Menon: Exposed kvcache.compression.entropy_threshold and documented it in docs/arch/collectives.md. Benchmarks updated to show sensitivity sweep.
Lena Wong: CI emulation looks good. Please ensure the fallback path is exercised in our nightly matrix for older drivers.
Ravi Menon: Added nightly job entry 'compat-legacy-driver' that runs NCCL-only path to keep coverage.
Asha Patel: Approved after addressing the tombstone/reclamation window and metrics additions.
notes: Opt-in feature: default off in hosted for now; internal customers can request early access.
Will iterate on eviction policy after 30-day field trial; plan to add cross-model sharing heuristics if stable.
release_notes: Experimental: NVSHMEM-backed shared KV slab + staged allreduce bridge to reduce inter-node KV latency for tensor-parallel inference. Opt-in via --enable-nvshmem-kvcache. Falls back to NCCL when unsupported.
performance_summary: 8x16 TP small-shard latency: median -18% p99 -22%; RLHF-chat throughput +14%; network egress -11% on small-shard workloads.
